author: GamingBolt
description:
At its heart, Onimusha: Way of the Sword makes its combat systems force you to embody the very perfection that Musashi strives for by turning it into a crucial pillar of its combat and progression. 

You’re encouraged to use every move you have, in different ways based on the situation, and against different enemies who come with their own twists for you to keep in mind.
title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword Sold a Million Copies in ONE Day, And This Is the Biggest Reason Why

author: GamingBolt
description:
It was only a matter of time before we tested DLSS 5 out on a selection of games to see if all the hype around it is justified. With two test systems running a curated list of games from across modern gaming history, we saw what it can do, what it does well, what it doesn’t, and a few things it wasn’t supposed to do, but did anyway. 

Of course, the first thing we did with our findings after we made sense of them was to put down everything we learned for you to check out.

Strap in as we take a trip spanning several attractive destinations in modern gaming, each of which got the DLSS 5 treatment with varying results. Does it make things better, or is it taking too much away from artistic interpretations of the games its working on? Join us and find out.
title: DLSS 5 Is Blowing My Mind, And That’s Slightly Terrifying

author: GamingBolt
description:
After briefly marauding the forests as both human and vampire in Blood of the Dawnwalker, you arrive at Svartrau, Vale Sangora’s only walled-in city. Dense with houses, parapets, and towers, visiting as a human during the day means exploring the streets, alleyways, and alcoves on foot. 

Yet, return as vampire Coen once the sun sets, and you gain a suite of traversal tools. Those rooftops? Walkable. A parapet? Climbable. The chimney? You can certainly scale them; a view outside the city walls is your reward for embracing your vampiric abilities.
title: Why Over A Million Gamers Are ADDICTED To The Blood of Dawnwalker
